content.document_focus: Guideline text on management and investigation of MINOCA (myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries) and related acute coronary syndromes.
abbreviations_listed: MINOCA (myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries)
NTpro BNP (N terminal pro brain natriuretic peptide)
content.initial_assessment_recommendations: Patients presenting with STEMI proceed directly to catheter lab. When non-obstructive coronary arteries are identified, further assessment should be considered. Patients with NSTE-ACS or UA are often stabilized on the ward prior to transfer.
content.investigations_examples: Potential blood tests: full blood count, renal profile, troponin, C-reactive protein, D-dimer, NT-pro BNP. CT scan of the brain considered if intracranial bleed suspected.
content.imaging_recommendations: If underlying cause of MINOCA is not established using functional coronary angiography, non-invasive imaging (echocardiography, CMR, CT) is recommended as clinically appropriate. CMR is a key diagnostic tool and can identify the underlying cause in up to ~87% of patients with a working diagnosis of MINOCA; should be performed as soon as possible, ideally during index admission.
content.diagnosis_and_management_summary: Diagnosis of underlying cause of MINOCA enables targeted treatment. Secondary prevention should be considered for those with evidence of coronary atherosclerotic disease and to control risk factors. Takotsubo management is largely supportive and empiric; myocarditis treatment covered in previous ESC documents. Ischemia with non-obstructive coronary arteries (INOCA) also described in context of CCS.
content.references_and_supplements: Multiple guideline citations and supplementary data referenced (including Table S13 and Recommendation Table 13).
content.notes: The page is a clinical guideline excerpt; it lists commonly used tests and imaging modalities and emphasizes using CMR early to maximize diagnostic yield.
